title: Concatenating counter spans
statement: Let $k$ be a natural number, let $\Gamma$ and $S$ be types, let $x$ be a finite input word over $\Gamma$, and let $H$ be a machine with $k+1$ work tapes and states of the counter-loop form over $S$. For an initial configuration $z$, natural times $s,t$, an integer counter position $cp$, a natural width, and predicates $R_1,R_2,R$ on the positions of the first $k$ work heads, suppose the run from $z$ spans time $s$ with invariant $R_1$, and the run from its time-$s$ configuration spans time $t$ with invariant $R_2$. If each of $R_1$ and $R_2$ implies $R$, then the run from $z$ spans time $s+t$ with invariant $R$: it avoids both exit anchors before that time, keeps the final work-head position in the interval from $cp-1$ to $cp+\mathrm{width}$ at every time up to it, and satisfies $R$ for the first $k$ head positions throughout.
